title: The Ultimate Desktop Laser? Creality Falcon A1 Pro Setup & Review
description:
👉 Buy NOW! Use code Shiny15 to get 15% OFF https://geni.us/FalconA1ProDirect (Affiliate Link)
👉 Buy on Amazon https://geni.us/Creality-Falcon-A1-Pro (Affiliate Link)
If you've been wanting to get into laser engraving but have been intimidated by the steep learning curve, the safety hazards, or the messy cables Creality Falcon A1 Pro might just be the right choice for you!

I have put this machine through its paces, testing both the 20W Blue Diode laser and the optional 2W Infrared (IR) module to see if it lives up to the hype and justifies the price tag.

🛡️ CLASS 1 SAFETY & ENCLOSED DESIGN
One of the biggest selling points of the Falcon A1 Pro is its form factor. It is a completely enclosed unit featuring an Eye-Protection Cover that filters out 99% of harmful laser light.

⚡ 20W DIODE + 2W IR = ULTIMATE VERSATILITY
The A1 Pro utilizes a brilliant modular laser system so you can swap tool heads based on your material.

20W Blue Semiconductor Laser (455nm): This is your daily workhorse. It can cut through 10mm basswood or 8mm black acrylic in a single pass. It easily hits speeds of up to 600mm/s, making it three times faster than older generation diode lasers.

2W IR Solid-State Laser (1064nm): This is where things get really fun. If you want to engrave bare metals (like gold, silver, brass, or aluminum), ceramics, or plastics without melting them, you swap in the IR module.

🧠 AI CAMERA & AUTO-FOCUS MAGIC
The Falcon A1 Pro features a top-mounted HD wide-angle camera. In the software, you get a live top-down preview of your entire workspace. You just drag and drop your design exactly where you want it on your material. Using the AI camera combined with a red-dot laser, the Z-axis it adjusts to the height to get to work faster!

📱 STANDALONE SMART FEATURES
The A1 Pro features a built-in smartphone-style touchscreen and Wi-Fi capability. You can slice your files, send them to the machine, and control the entire job directly from the Creality App while sitting on the couch.

🛠️ THE SETUP EXPERIENCE & SOFTWARE ECOSYSTEM
The unboxing experience is remarkably painless. Creality markets this as a "One Minute Unbox," and while that might be a slight exaggeration, it arrives about 80% pre-assembled. You aren't spending hours assembling everything. You simply pull it out of the box, plug in the exhaust hose, connect the power, and you are ready to engrave.

On the software side, the Falcon A1 Pro is fully compatible with LightBurn and LaserGRBL, which is a massive plus for experienced makers who already have their workflows dialed in. However, Creality also includes their own Falcon Design Space software. While it might lack some of the ultra-advanced node-editing features of LightBurn, it integrates seamlessly with the machine's Wi-Fi capabilities and top-down camera. For beginners, Falcon Design Space takes the headache out of the process, offering an intuitive UI that gets you from an image file to a finished physical product in minutes.

🔍 FINAL VERDICT: IS IT WORTH IT?
If you are someone who wants to tinker with the machine itself, build your own enclosure, and save a few bucks, a barebones open-frame laser might still be your best bet. But if you value your time, your eyesight, and your lung health, the Falcon A1 Pro is a premium machine that delivers. It transforms laser engraving from an intimidating garage project into a polished, living-room-friendly appliance. Whether you are starting an Etsy shop for custom leather patches, engraving Yeti cups, or just want the ultimate maker tool on your desk, this dual-laser system delivers professional results with consumer-level ease of use.

It’s opal cutting time!

This parcel came from our secret opal mine and it’s some of the best rough we’ve found to date, showing that elusive red fire we’re always chasing. 

First step was sorting out what I wanted to cut, I used my newly engraved opal sorting board thanks to Creality who sent over the laser engraver for me to have a go on! Love the falcon a1 laser engraver! 

I then sent the opal under the cutting wheels to reveal the gems hiding in the rough. 

In the rough, I’d estimate this parcel would’ve sold for around $1,500 as a small jar. That might not sound huge, but it shows the real potential of this ground. If we were to pull a few kilos of this quality which is absolutely possible it could turn into a seriously exciting find.

The material did prove a bit tricky to cut, with smaller colour bars to work around, but overall I’m really happy with the stones we managed to get out of it.

After weighing the finished stones and working out a rough price per carat, I estimate the total value of the cut stones could be around $7,000. Some of these will be set into jewellery, while others will be sold as cut stones.

title: Creality Sermoon S1 3D Scanner | The Fastest Scanner I Have Ever Used
description:
In this video I'll be testing out and reviewing the Creality Sermoon S1 3D Scanner. The Sermoon S1 is the fastest scanner I have used so far and features multiple laser modes. It has 34 blue laser lines for quick scanning, 7 parallel lines for high detail scanning, and a single blue laser line for scanning deep holes and pockets. It also features an NIR mode for scanning without the need for markers and a color RGB camera for capturing color detail. While this scanner does connect through a USB cord, there is an optional Scan Bridge accessory that you can purchase separately in order to scan wirelessly. As far as the price goes, this is more expensive than other models but I think it's worth it for the quick scanning alone. At 90FPS, this 3D scanner blows away every other scanner I've used when it comes to speed. The detail came out fantastic on all the scans I tested out and I also rarely lost tracking. Which if some of you know, can be a big problem with some of the other 3D scanners on the market.  If you're looking for a 3d scanner that is more for professional use, captures high detail with high speed, and is very simple to use, I would definitely recommend looking into this one.

My experience with the A1 Pro was pretty seamless. It arrived fully assembled and only required a few minutes to plug in and get going. It paired with my computer over wifi, and after perusing the included software for a few minutes I was ready to start cutting and engraving. The learning curve was pretty quick, as I have never worked with any device like this before and only ran into a couple of beginner issues that didn't actually affect the end product! My mistakes can be your knowledge: for one: don't use a spoil board under your work piece! If you want to preserve the bed of your A1 Pro, put a spoil board UNDER the honeycomb grill. I didn't know and it got a little too smoky and the machine paused to let me know there was a possible fire. Luckily there was not! I can see this tool being useful for many future endeavours, including inlays, cutting out acoustic guitar repair components like cleats, making router templates for pickups, bodies, amp grills and making pick guards. It is so much faster than the hand work that I always use for such tasks and will cut down on a lot of hand work time and let me get to other less tedious tasks! All in all and very handy tool. My only complaint: the software isn't 100% intuitive and the camera is a bit of a fish eye lens which does not give a realistic portrayal of where the cuts will actually occur on the material. My suggestion is that, on future models, the camera be attached to the same mechanism as the laser module so that unit can scan the surface and give a 1:1 representation of the work surface to use in the layout program.

title: Reverse Engineering a Custom Part for Resin 3D Printing
description:

#autodeskad #HeyGears #Reflex2 #HeyGearsReflex2 #autodeskfusion360 #fusion360 #Creality #Creality3DScanner #3dscanning #3dmodel #3dscanner #RaptorPro

I've been making the Audi R8 fascia kit for several years by casting it in resin into silicone moulds. This video demonstrates the workflow and transition from manufacturing fascia using silicone moulds to resin printing. Silicone moulds have a limited lifespan, and the mould needs to be remade after a certain number of casts. Transferring to a resin-printed workflow has many benefits, including reduced labour as there's no mould to remake, component consistency between prints, and broader material choices.

To achieve this, I scanned the master fascia I had hand-made using the Creality Raptor Pro scanner, reverse-engineered it in Fusion 360, and then printed it on the HeyGears Reflex 2. Now that I have a 3D model of the fascia, I can also mirror it, allowing me to easily and accurately create a left-hand drive version without needing a left-hand drive vehicle to test the fit.

title: 12,000 PLN for a Toyota after a tree? See what condition it's in.
description:
🤝 Contact: wterenie4x4off@gmail.com

A Toyota crashed into a tree at about 60 km/h—instead of scrapping it, I'm stripping it down to the bare frame and trying to straighten something a normal workshop wouldn't attempt. The frame's side member has gone sideways and down, the frame is warped, the body is stressed, the axle is retracted... and I want to turn this Toyota into a proper off-roader again. In this episode, you'll see the entire process: removing the body, measuring the frame with compasses, buying a second donor frame, cutting and joining the two frames, sandblasting the inside of the frame, and 3D scanning it to make it easier to fabricate parts in the future. Finally, I'll be announcing the maintenance and assembly of the axles.

If you're interested in rebuilding salvage vehicles, repairing frames, building 4x4s from pre-made and "mixed" parts, or just want to see if a salvaged Toyota even makes sense – this is the place to do it, no bullshit.

title: Uncovering my forgotten project car: A 1970's KE25 Corolla | Revopoint Miraco Plus 3D Scanner
description:
Miraco Plus Affiliate link: http://shrsl.com/2qkrc-2frb-133hz #revopoint  #miracoplus 
Discount code: REVOPRFLCT

At what point would you say that a project car is "too far gone"? I wouldn't quite call this a classic car restoration and to be honest I only bought this project car shell on a whim for some of the spares it came with, but after giving it more thought over time I've decided that it would in-fact be the perfect base for designing a bunch of parts for both the KE25 and the KE70 corollas.
Once I've put in the effort of designing all of these extra bits and pieces, I can also use the beauty of creating with CAD, which is repeatability. I'd easily be able to reprint and utilise a whole bunch of the parts and I also wouldn't feel too bad about cutting a lot of this car up - as it's already pretty rough!
I've got a whole bunch of spare silvia parts that I also couldn't really think of much of a use for - so this is a perfect opportunity to utilise them as well.

The best 3D printed car parts are yet to come, with the design for the dash, center console and other interior parts and I think having the bare shell will make it a lot easier to show and measure up a whole bunch of new "how to" 3d model for 3d printing and design 3d printable objects.

title: Can This Laser Engraver Make Awesome Art? Creality Falcon A1
description:
Creality Falcon A1

👉 Subscribe Falcon Laser Official YouTube: https://crealityfalcon-laser.com/4in4...


In this video, I get hands-on with the Creality Falcon A1 10W Laser Engraver & Cutter and put it through a bunch of real projects. I used LightBurn for all my tests because it’s my go-to, but the Falcon A1 also works with Falcon Design Space (which is great with the built-in camera) and LaserGRBL.

Here’s what I made:

Material Test on 2 mm Plywood – I set up a 10×10 grid, running power from 10% to 100% and speeds from 100 mm/min to 1000 mm/min. This showed exactly what this machine can do for clean cuts and crisp engraving.

Engraving on a Black Aluminium Card – The detail was unreal. The fine 0.06 × 0.08 mm laser spot made it look super sharp.

Large 20×20 cm Plywood Engraving – A big piece, but the quality stayed consistent all the way across thanks to the CoreXY motion system.

Matt Colour Acrylic Engraving – This one came out beautifully, with that nice frosted look on the acrylic surface.

Mechanical Coffee Coaster (3 mm Coated Plywood) – Every part fit perfectly after cutting—no sanding needed.

Falcon A1–Themed Wall Clock (3 mm Plywood) – This one was all cutting, no engraving. I spray-painted the pieces to give it some extra style.

Why I like the Falcon A1:

Comes fully assembled and enclosed, so it’s safe to use right away.

Class 1 Laser Safety Certified – has tinted covers that block 99% of the laser light, a lid-open stop, and an emergency button.

Built-in HD camera – lets you see and position your design exactly where you want it on your material.

Auto material recognition – with QR cards to quickly set up the right settings.

CoreXY motion system – up to 600 mm/s speed and 0.01 mm accuracy, so it’s fast and super precise.

10W laser power with a tiny spot size for detailed engraving and clean cuts on wood, acrylic, leather, coated metals, and more.

Air assist & smoke extraction built in—keeps edges clean and the workspace clear.

Everything I made in this video was done with LightBurn, but if you’re new to laser engraving, Falcon Design Space is also really beginner-friendly, especially with that camera preview.

title: Creality Falcon A1 Pro Review in 57 Seconds
description:
🔥 Grab the Creality Falcon A1 Pro here:
https://geni.us/CrealityFalconA1Pro

The Creality Falcon A1 Pro is a laser engraver that shouldn’t work this well—but it does. This dual-laser machine combines a 20W diode and a 2W infrared laser into one compact desktop unit that can engrave stainless steel, burn wood, cut acrylic, and mark leather without breaking a sweat. In this Short, I put it through a real-world test with no marketing fluff—just raw footage of it doing what it claims to do.

If you're new to laser engraving or looking to upgrade from a budget machine, the Falcon A1 Pro offers an oddly satisfying mix of chaos and capability. It’s beginner-friendly in theory, thanks to autofocus, built-in air assist, and a top-down preview camera. It works with USB or Wi-Fi, and supports rotary engraving for curved objects like tumblers. The working area is 318x305mm, giving plenty of room for custom gifts, production jobs, and creative mayhem.

Unlike most diode engravers, the Falcon A1 Pro includes an IR laser module, which allows it to engrave metal directly—no marking sprays or coatings required. You can burn crisp text into anodised aluminium, etch branding into stainless steel, and engrave onto coated plastics without resorting to hacks. For wood, leather, and acrylic, the 20W diode is fast, sharp, and delivers excellent contrast and depth, especially when paired with air assist.

And yet… it's still a Creality machine. The software is basic, the UI is clunky, and the camera calibration process feels like a puzzle with missing instructions. Wi-Fi drops unexpectedly, and LightBurn setup isn’t plug-and-play unless you’re comfortable with device profiles. Still, when you get it going, it’s fun. It burns beautifully. It cuts quickly. It’s janky, but it delivers.

This isn’t just a tool for hobbyists. It’s a small business weapon. You can use it to personalise coasters, engrave leather wallets, mark tumblers, customise phone cases, or cut wood signage. If you're starting an Etsy shop, selling engraved gifts at craft markets, or running a side hustle out of your garage, this machine gets the job done. It’s fast enough for light production, accurate enough for fine detail, and cheap enough to justify without needing a bank loan.

And yes, it works with LightBurn—once set up, it unlocks far better control over power, speed, and positioning than the default Falcon Design Suite software. LightBurn also helps mitigate some of the awkward UI moments from the touchscreen panel, which hides useful features like homing in the weirdest places. Use LightBurn and you’ll see what this machine is really capable of.

One thing I won’t shut up about is safety. The Falcon A1 Pro is marketed as a Class 1 device, and the orange shield is supposed to block laser radiation—but don’t risk your eyes on a promise. I strongly recommend wearing OD6+ laser safety glasses every time, especially when engraving reflective surfaces like stainless steel. I had a scare, and it’s not worth it. Be smart.

This Short is just a tease. The full review on my channel dives deeper—showing how the A1 Pro performs across dozens of materials, how to calibrate the camera, how to fix annoying software quirks, and where this machine falls short. I cover everything you’d wish you knew before buying: what’s included, what works out of the box, and what still feels like a public beta.

Compared to other laser engravers like the xTool D1 Pro, Atomstack X30, and Ortur Laser Master 3, the Falcon A1 Pro is less refined but just as capable. It’s chaotic, powerful, and weirdly addictive. It’s not the most professional experience, but the end results are often indistinguishable from machines that cost much more. It’s one of those tools that keeps you coming back—even after it annoys the hell out of you.

If you want to engrave gifts, burn logos into wood, cut custom acrylic signs, etch metal tags, or start a small engraving business from your shed, the Falcon A1 Pro might be exactly what you didn’t know you needed. It won’t hold your hand. But it will push you to get creative—and that’s the point.

Are you considering the Creality Falcon2 Pro 60W laser engraver for your business, side hustle, or home workshop? In this comprehensive hands-on review, I walk you through everything you need to know about the Falcon 2 Pro—from unboxing to setup, common issues, performance with various materials, and real-world workspace improvements. If you're trying to decide whether this powerful diode laser is right for you, this video lays out the pros, the cons, and the upgrades that can make all the difference when looking at laser engraver, laser cutter and laser ethcher.

The Creality Falcon 2 Pro is one of the most powerful diode laser engravers available, offering up to 60 watts of output. That much power opens the door to faster cutting speeds, deeper engravings, and the ability to process much thicker materials than traditional 10W or 20W diode lasers. However, raw power alone isn’t enough—you also need reliability, usability, and support. That’s why I stress-tested this machine under real conditions, including high temperatures in a non-air-conditioned garage where outside temps reached 120°F.

During this deep-dive, I cover everything from software configuration to airflow optimization, and even tips to make the laser more user-friendly. You’ll learn how I overcame several initial frustrations, including a misalignment issue caused by the default workspace origin in Falcon Design Space. If you’re using a Mac, I also share my experience with USB connection reliability compared to Windows and what I did to resolve repeated disconnection issues.

One of the most confusing but critical features is the Falcon 2 Pro’s multi-mode precision setting. This setting lets you toggle between Precise, Normal, and Powerful laser modes via a top-mounted button. However, the machine doesn’t remember your last mode after powering off. In this video, I show you how to set the default power level at startup using the $156= console command—something Creality support didn’t include in the manual but confirmed works reliably:

$156=1 for Precise (1 LED)
$156=2 for Normal (2 LEDs)
$156=3 for Powerful (3 LEDs)

In my shop, I also had challenges with the included slat bed. It works, but because it’s not magnetic, materials would sometimes shift or lift up when removing tape. My wife had a brilliant solution—she used white fingernail polish to draw alignment borders directly on the slats, making material positioning easier and faster. Later, I added the official Creality honeycomb bed, which is magnetic, and now it works beautifully for holding materials firmly in place with magnets. If you plan to do frequent cuts or production work, this is one upgrade I highly recommend.

Heat management was another big concern. With summer temperatures soaring in the garage, I did have the Falcon 2 Pro overheat once during a long engraving job. That moment really worried me. After consulting Creality support, I relocated the unit closer to a 12,000 BTU portable air conditioner, and since keeping the ambient temperature consistently below 90°F, I haven’t had any additional issues. This video covers exactly how I solved the problem, step by step.

If you're considering using this machine indoors, you’ll also want to watch the section where I talk about smoke and fume control. The built in exhaust fan helps, but I strongly suggest using the official Creality Falcon Smoke Purifier if you can’t pipe the exhaust outdoors. Without a purifier or a modified exhaust route, using this indoors may result in unpleasant fumes or long-term air quality issues.

Performance-wise, the Falcon 2 Pro easily handles a wide range of materials. The 60W output means you’ll need fewer passes for most materials, and edges are cleaner with less scorching.

In this video, I restore an old tobacco cutting machine that had seen better days. Many of the wooden parts were broken or missing, so I recreated them using my laser cutter and reinforced them with toothpicks for added strength. The main aluminum frame was cleaned and reworked, and I pressed in new custom-made brass bearings.

All shafts were remade from scratch on the lathe and nickel-plated for durability. I also forged two brand new blades from high carbon tool steel — annealed, shaped, and then hardened to restore their cutting power.

The worn gears were sandblasted, faced on the lathe, polished, and nickel-plated. Finally, the original wooden handle was carefully restored and fitted with a new brass end cap to support the new shaft.

We also continue working on the veggie garden and bring in extra mulch to cover all the paths, making the space tidier and more practical. As soon as the sun starts to go down, we head back outside to continue our work in the vegetable garden.

The Creality Falcon A1 10W Laser Engraver & Cutter is a powerful and beginner-friendly machine that offers advanced features in a compact and ready-to-use package. It comes equipped with a 10W diode laser and supports engraving speeds of up to 600mm/s, thanks to its fast CoreXY motion system. The working area measures approximately 381 × 305 mm (around 15 × 12 inches), and it delivers precise results with an ultra-fine laser spot size of 0.06 × 0.08 mm.

One of the standout aspects of the Falcon A1 is its plug-and-play setup. It arrives pre-assembled, making it easy for first-time users to get started quickly. The machine also includes a smart AI camera that enables live previews, auto-positioning, and precise contour tracing for repeatable, batch engraving workflows. A major highlight is the auto-material recognition system, which automatically detects the type of material being used and adjusts the laser parameters accordingly—removing much of the guesswork and reducing material waste.

The enclosed design prioritizes safety, featuring a tempered glass lid, emergency stop button, flame detection, and a door-open auto-shutdown system. It meets Class-1 safety standards and is certified with FDA, CE, and RoHS compliance, making it safe for home and workshop environments.

Inside the box, you'll find everything you need to get started, including the main unit, exhaust hose, air-assist module, silicone tubing, power supply, calibration tools, a sample basswood board, USB cables, rotary kit connection cable, and basic tools like a brush and Allen wrench.

In terms of performance, the Falcon A1 has received high praise for its ease of use and strong results right out of the box. It supports design platforms such as LightBurn, LaserGRBL, and Creality's own Falcon Design Space. Reviewers highlight that the machine is capable of cleanly cutting through up to 1/4-inch plywood and even 3/8-inch white oak, which is impressive for a 10W unit. The air assist and enclosure significantly improve cutting depth and quality.

Users on platforms like Reddit and YouTube frequently note that the Falcon A1 brings together several premium features—camera-guided positioning, air assist, an enclosure, and auto-recognition—in a single, integrated machine. It's priced competitively, especially when compared to standalone systems requiring add-ons to achieve similar results.

The main drawbacks mentioned include the lack of a built-in honeycomb bed for cutting support, which may need to be purchased separately. Additionally, while the Falcon A1 excels at working with wood, acrylic, leather, and similar materials, it is not designed for cutting metal.

Overall, the Creality Falcon A1 is an ideal choice for beginners, DIYers, and makers who want to get into laser engraving with minimal setup, reliable performance, and strong safety features. It's particularly well-suited for engraving detailed designs on a wide variety of materials and provides a smooth on-ramp for creators looking to explore laser cutting for the first time.

The scanner tested is the Creality Scan Raptor Pro, which adds the 22 cross laser line mode as well as a large object distance over the Creality Scan Raptor.

For the files that were shown in the video, you can download them from these Fusion links.  The files have been aligned in QuickSurface Lite.  

KTM Bar Clamp - This part was scanned with Parallel Laser lines in 4 scans.  The part is clear anodized machined aluminum.
https://a360.co/4jGRIJ3

GSXR Triple Clamp - This part is cast aluminum with the bottom being a rough cast and the top being hand sanded.  its "shiny" but not a mirror shine.  The top was scanned in cross laser line mode and the bottom in parallel line mode.  As mentioned in the video some of the marker dots weren't removed so there was some post processing that happened in QuickSurface.  You can see the lower facet count in areas I patched.

https://a360.co/3HHZipy

Starion Transmission - This file contains 3 meshes.  The entire transmission and workbench were scanned in Large NIR mode with no processing after the "1 click" processing in CrealityScan (other than aligning them in QS Lite.  The medium scan is only a portion of the transmission in an area with bolts and a casting "5".  The small scan is just this area with bolts and the "5"  .  The 1 click mesh processing tries to seal the scans as "water tight" so areas that were missed during the scan have a weird fill.  But hopefully this will show the difference in detail between small, medium, and large.

Hi guys, today I built a machine based on the idea of ​​turning snails into real artists. In fact, what better artist than a snail to create a work of art in a completely non-discriminatory and impartial way?

The idea is to exploit the position of the snail's body and then determine its position using a potentiometer. In this case, I'd say the simplest and most precise way to control a brush is to use stepper motors. These motors guarantee optimal precision and advance in small steps, as the name suggests, thanks to a frequency generator. This frequency generator is capable of sending small pulses that then control a driver. The driver will then have the function of supplying all the electrical power to the motor itself. In short, my idea is to intervene on the frequency itself, so the snails will not alter the motor's power (i.e., the voltage and AMP radius of the motor itself), but will simply vary the generated frequency with the position of their bodies. This is much safer for the snail. In fact, this PWM signal generator uses only 2 V to generate these small pulses, which are certainly a very low voltage and very safe to work with in any case. I want to electrically isolate the snails from my entire electronic circuit in any way possible. To do this, I took a thin cotton thread, which has an important property: it acts as an electrical insulator.

Frequencies to vary the frequency. The circuit calculates the resistance value of the potentiometer. In short, the potentiometer in this circuit functions like a real accelerator for our car.

So, the less resistance there is, the faster and more frequent the frequency will be, and vice versa.

Now all that's left is to study a system to create My potentiometer with my resistance value so I can determine the position of the snails using this potentiometer.

You know how much I love making my own analog projects without having to write code with Arduino, and I think this is the simplest method.

After studying that a snail weighing about 20 g can lift 20 g without any problem, a very logical deduction considering that a snail can walk vertically up a wall without tiring.

I built a glass chemistry test tube containing distilled water with very little salt.

This liquid will act as a variable resistance, and the snail's body itself will attempt to move a counterweight within the fluid.

The further the counterweight is moved, the more the resistance will vary, and consequently, the frequency generator will accelerate or accelerate the stepper motor.

And I was truly amazed by the precision and cutting speed of this 10 W

I then mounted everything on a solid plywood table.

In total, I had four moving parts on the table: a central gear that rotates very slowly, about 1 rpm.

We have another gear that also rotates very slowly, about 4 rpm.
And we have the other two gears, which I've noticed work best if they have roughly the same rotation speed, about 10 rpm.

Hello Everyone,

In this video I take a first look at the Creality Falcon A1 laser machine.  
This is a 10w machine, but don't be put off by it's limited power.  Lower powered machines have a finer 'kerf', which requires less power to cut through materials.  I think this machine would be ideal for a scale model maker, and in the video I try to show a variety of outcomes which I think reflect what viewers of this channel might be interested in.

Creality have also released the Falcon Design Space software with this machine which can be downloaded for free from the link below.  I'm just scratching the surface of this innovative approach to laser cutting so will save the deep-dive for a future video, but it enables smart material identification and sets the power and speed functions automatically, greatly increasing productivity and reducing waste in addition to demystifying the whole process for a beginner. 

I'm happy to answer any questions or try suggestions out for the benefit of viewers so feel free to ask away in the comments.
This machine was supplied for testing at no cost to me, and I've not been paid to make the video.  My thoughts are my own, and my opinions honest.
I will have the machine on display and working as part of my demos at forthcoming modelling exhibitions (Scalefour Crewe in June and Scaleforum in September), and I'd encourage anyone interested to come along and take a look, and have a play yourself.
I think this is a great tool.  I'd even go further and say it's the best machine of its type which I've used as it's easy to set-up, efficient and quiet in use.

In this Video I restored an old 'Solex' or 'VeloSolex' Moped. Theyre known as the first E-Bikes - a bike with a support engine. 
In this video, I'll take you on a journey through the restoration of a Solex, a true classic of the 70s. From the first step of the repair to the final test drive, I'll show you how I brought this vintage moped project to life.

First, I repaired the plastic parts, which had suffered considerable wear and tear over the years. I cut, lasered, welded, filled, and repainted the parts! Now they shine like new again.

In the next step, I re-chromed the metal parts using pin electroplating to preserve the Solex's typical retro look. The glossy surface adds the finishing touch to the restoration.

I made the new wooden handlebar grips myself on the lathe. Special attention was paid to ensuring they fit perfectly into the overall look, both functionally and visually.

For the footrest, I used a particularly cool process – a laser cutter to cut the wooden parts. The result is a precisely crafted footrest that adds even more character to the Solex.

Finally, it was time to assemble the Solex. After all the parts were restored and machined, it was time to put the whole thing together and bring the Solex to life.

Finally, there's a test drive to see how well the Solex runs after the restoration.

🛠️ HOW IT WAS MADE

I had wanted to make a leather map of Middle Earth for a very long time. My wife is a huge Tolkien fan, she has all the books, and we are both fans of the films - so this one started as a Christmas gift, made early for once.

Sheepskin, brown leather dye, neatsfoot oil, a touch of antique finish and Tan-Kote. The map file came from the internet months earlier and almost nothing was ready for engraving: the roads, the shorelines and the trees all had to be reworked, and I removed most of the cities and the small details that would never have read on leather. The place names are set in the Hobbiton font, and it took a lot of test passes to find the right laser settings.

title: Making My Simplest Wallet Even Simpler w/ a Laser!   #CrealityFalcon #lasercutting #laserengraving
description:
20% off with code "CFWIN20"
https://shareasale.com/u.cfm?d=110578...

I designed this wallet to be very simple to make. Basically, you cut a rectangular piece of leather, use the same punch to cut all the slots and then punch the stitching holes and stitch it up. But I wanted to see if I could use my new @crealityfalcon 2 Pro laser to do everything but the stitching. So I created and imported a template into Lightburn and then it was off to the laser. The enclosed 22W laser with all its amazing safety features as well as the included air assist made cutting the wallet and the stitching holes super quick and safe and it came out perfect and ready to stitch. Next, I simply glued the wallet together, lining up the precise stitching holes. Then I quickly stitched up each side before doing some quick edge finishing. And just like that, I had made my simplest card wallet even simpler using my new Creality Falcon2 Pro laser! As always, thanks for watching!

I took the Creality Ferret Pro 3D Scanner for a spin. I scanned various items as a beginner 3D scanner user to see what would work well and what doesn't. It turns out, the best objects to scan are sculptures of at least 6" cubed. Things that have narrow gemoetries doesn't do so well. Also large objects would need some anchor points so that it can keep a lock on the 3D space while scanning.

title: Creating My Digital Self Into A Game Character To Use In Fortnite
description:
In this exciting journey, I’m taking you behind the scenes as I transform myself into a fully-fledged game character for use in Fortnite. From scanning my own head to capturing facial expressions and motion, every step is an adventure!

Creality Ferret Pro Head Scan:
I kick things off by using the Creality Ferret Pro 3D scanner to capture an accurate representation of my own head. This high-resolution scan will serve as the foundation for my digital avatar.
Character Creator 4 Customization:

Next, I dive into Character Creator 4, where I meticulously craft my character’s appearance. From facial features to clothing and accessories, I’m turning myself into a unique Fortnite-ready persona.

Rokoko HeadRig Facial Motion Capture:
The Rokoko Head Ring comes into play as I record my facial expressions and movements. This cutting-edge technology ensures that my in-game character emotes just like I do in real life.

iClone for Final Motion Capture:
iClone takes center stage as I bring my character to life. Using motion capture, I create dynamic animations.

Fortnite UEFN:
Finally, I merged all the elements in Unreal Engine (UEFN). This powerful game engine allows me to seamlessly blend my character with the Fortnite environment, making them a part of the epic “Battle for Wu-York City.”

⚠️SDカードの初期化で困ったこと共有

・FAT32でフォーマットする
・アロケーションユニットサイズを4096B（バイト）にする
・MACだとコマンド（ターミナルアプリ等）でしかフォーマットできない

コマンド（ターミナル.app等）で初期化するのも癖あり。
・ディスク一覧でSDカードのディスク確認→diskutil list
・SDカードをアンマウント（diskutil listで確認した"disk4s1"等のIDを${ID}に入れてね）→unmount /dev/${ID}
・SDカードフォーマット→sudo newfs_msdos -v ${SDカードの任意の名前} -b 4096 /dev/${ID}
・SDカードをマウント→diskutil mountDisk /dev/disk4s1

この手順でフォーマットすればレーザー彫刻機のSDカードスロットで読み取り可能になります。
ファームウェアアップデートのときに必要だと思うので備忘録。 

⚠️パソコンと接続するときに困ったこと共有

最初USB-Cケーブルでパソコンとレーザー彫刻機を接続しましたが、
彫刻ソフト（LightBurn）に接続ポートが表示されず。
LightBurnのヘルプページ見つけて解決しました。

・パソコン本体側に接続するUSBポートは、"USB-A"タイプに繋ぐ
・USB-C端子しか付いてないMACの場合は、USBハブでUSB-Aを経由させる

【レーザー彫刻機、カメラ】(type-Cメス)←→【USBハブ】(type-Aメス)←(type-Aオス)【USBケーブル】(type-Cオス)→(type-Cメス)【MACパソコン】

All sponsored content in my videos are my own viewpoints and I am allowed to speak freely about what I did and did not like about the product. I never recommend a product to my audience that I wouldn’t regularly use myself.

After using the Falcon2 Pro 40W for a few weeks here are my thoughts:

Pros:
Large working area
The 40W laser is fast and can cut up to 0.75” thick in a large variety of materials in a single pass
Fully enclosed setup is safer for you and the environment than wearing laser safety glasses alone
Camera system allows for amazingly precise setups for your cuttings/engravings
Multiple laser power settings (1.5W, 22W, and 40W) for ultra precision

Cons:
Assembly instructions could be a little clearer (Creality YouTube videos did help)
Expensive, although on par with other laser units of similar sizes
An additional system ($) is required to manage and control the smoke exhaust once it leaves the laser system
The laser bed surface rails are a bit shaky during quick laser movements
No homegrown software solution, relies on third party software to operate (which are still very good!)

title: Cortador y grabador láser: cómo funciona y para qué nos sirve (Bricocrack)
description:
Trabajamos con una cortadora y grabadora láser sobre madera y metal para que veas cómo funciona y si te puede servir para tus proyectos de bricolador o maker.
https://www.bricocrack.tv. Tutorial Bricolaje Making Herramientas Cortadora láser Grabadora láser. El cortador y grabador láser que utilizamos en este vídeo es de Creality Falcon.

Si quieres comprar online el Cortador y Grabador Creality Falcon2 Pro con un CUPÓN DE DESCUENTO, pincha en este enlace: https://s.zbanx.com/r/lyTpXd5FYF70

Aquí encontrarás más información sobre el cortador y grabador Creality Falcon2 Pro:    / @falconlaserofficial  .

La ropa de trabajo y el calzado de seguridad que lleva Juan Mateos en este vídeo son de Velilla Group, entra en su web para conocer sus catálogos: https://www.velilla-group.com/.

Nuestro compañero Bosco ha estado haciendo pruebas con una cortadora láser para que podamos ver todos cómo funciona y qué partido le podemos sacar en el taller. Así, si estás pensando hacerte con una, viendo funcionar a esta Creality Falcon2 Pro que, además de cortar graba, te puedes hacer una idea más exacta de si es interesante incorporar esta herramienta en tu taller de bricolador o maker.  

Bosco comienza por describirte la máquina y todos los elementos que incluye: láser de 40 vatios, láser de 1,6 W, gafas de protección, compresor, ventilador, manguera de extracción, etc. Y nos comenta a continuación los elementos de seguridad que incorpora: llave de seguridad, freno de emergencia, cubierta protectora y distintos sensores y detectores diseñados para interrumpir su funcionamiento ante cualquier incidencia. 

El cortador y grabador de láser Creality Falcon2 Pro se puede controlar mediante una tarjeta micro SD que se introduce en la máquina o a través de un software que instalamos en nuestro ordenador. Nosotros hemos optado por instalarnos el software LightBurn y conectar el ordenador a la máquina con los cables que también están incluidos. 

Para mostrarte cómo funciona el cortador sobre madera, hemos preparado un pequeño proyecto: un dispensador de cintas para nuestro taller. Lo hemos hecho con contrachapado de 10 mm de espesor. Bosco te explica qué variables hay que tener en cuenta para conseguir estos ensambles de tipo dedo cortados con tantísima precisión: la potencia del láser, la velocidad de corte y el número de pasadas. 

Antes de poner la máquina a trabajar sobre cualquier material, tenemos que regular la altura de corte o de grabado. Para ello la máquina dispone una galga. También comprobamos que nuestro diseño está dentro del área de trabajo de la cortadora. La máquina nos lo muestra haciendo un recorrido por el perímetro y podemos verlo a través del software o de la propia cámara que lleva incorporada la Creality Falcon2 Pro.

Utilizamos otro tablero de contrachapado para cortar las ruedas que van a sujetar las cintas en el dispensador. Cortadas todas las piezas de madera, ya podemos ensamblar con cola blanca el cajón y montar nuestro dispensador.

Resumiendo, corte de madera muy preciso sin ruido ni polvo.

Vamos a ver ahora cómo funciona Creality Falcon2 Pro como grabador láser. Se puede grabar sobre una gran variedad de materiales como cristal, cuero, madera…Nosotros hemos elegido hacerlo sobre metal y hemos grabado el nombre de Bricocrack sobre uno de nuestros niveles de burbuja. ¡Mira qué bien queda! 😊

Para terminar, Bosco nos da su opinión sobre la máquina. Lo que más le ha sorprendido es la potencia para el corte, su precisión y, en conjunto, la calidad con que está construida para evitar la emisión de ruidos, polvo y humos.   

Esperamos que te haya resultado útil este tutorial para entender cómo funciona un cortador y grabador láser y que te ayude a tomar decisiones. Cuéntanoslo aquí abajo, en los comentarios del vídeo, porque tu opinión es siempre muy importante para nosotros. 

¡Muchas gracias anticipadas! 😊😊😊

In this video, we look at the Creality Falcon 2 Laser Engraver, a 22 Watt laser machine that stands head and shoulders above all other laser engraving machines.
The Creality Falon2 has enough power to cut through a thick piece of wood, but it is also capable of making detailed engravings. The laser comes with a very good quality Air Assist, which means that the Falcon2 is also able to cut very thin objects. The safety measures in the Creality Falcon2 are exceptional because this laser has many more sensors to detect problems than any other machine I've ever tested. For example, the Falcon 2 has a sensor to see if the lens is dirty, and another sensor to see how good the airflow to the air-assist nozzle is.
The Creality Falcon2 is certainly not a cheap machine, but it is the first diode laser engraving machine that can actually be used in a production environment, making it much better than other lasers that you should mainly see as hobby machines.

title: 🛠 Laser cutting Insulation material with the Creality Falcon 2
description:
During the renovation of my house, insulation material had to be adjusted in several places so that chimney pipes and air extraction pipes could be placed through the insulation material. Since it is very difficult to draw a perfect ellipse by hand, and even more difficult to cut it out with power tools, I used my Creality Falcon 2 laser engraver to create the holes. As a result, the holes are cut so cleanly and beautifully that it seems as if this was done directly in the factory of the insulation material.

The advantage of the Creality Falcon 2 compared to my other laser cutting machines is that the combination of the large power of 22 Watt and the perfect Air Assist make it possible to cut white sheet material without many burn marks being visible on the surface of the plate material.

Home the laser

description:
Based on the latest FAC spot compression technology, four powerful 6W laser diodes are compressed to increase the laser power to 22W. It can cut 15mm wood in one pass, cut 10mm black acrylic in one pass and cut aluminum sheet stainless steel with a thickness of 0.05 mm in one pass.
When the machine is engraving, the orange air-assist light is always on, when cutting, the green air-assist light should be on;
if the red light flashes while sculpting, please check:
1. Whether the air pump is connected to the machine.
2. that the knob switch on the left side of the machine is set to maximum.
3. that the silicone air tube above the laser module is connected and is not kinked.

title: Creality Falcon 2 22W: Up close look at engraving stainless steel, and must have enclosure accessory
description:
Creality sponsored this video by sending me the machine with accessories as payment for the video. This is my first time using a laser cutter/engraver before for me so no spectacular projects with it yet. Out of the three accessories, that enclosure is the best. Even cutting that small piece of wood with the door on the enclosure open, my garage stunk for a day of burnt wood. I can't imagine how bad it would smell after a couple hours cutting plywood! Enclosure for laser cutters is mandatory in my books for the safety it gives you.

I’m quite impressed with what it can do to stainless steel. With a higher wattage laser you could probably get in the territory of cutting thinner gauge stainless steel which would be amazing for projects. I’m sure it’ll blast through paper and felt like it wasn't there. I’m not interested in cutting any plastic due to the fumes.

Still trying to figure out something interesting I could do with the rotary accessory. For a small business, sticking your logo/brand on stainless steel water bottles would work out well in low volumes.

title: Powerful and Precise Creality Falcon2 40W. Cuts 39mm wood in one pass like  butter.
description:
Powerful and Precise Creality Falcon2 40W. Cuts 39mm wood in one pass like  butter.

Falcon2 22W Laser Engraver:https://tinyurl.com/mrxxnsvn

The Falcon2 is Creality's most powerful laser engraver to date. 
The Falcon2 40W incorporates a number of breakthrough features, such as adjustable spot adjustment for higher work efficiency and finer work details. This allows the Falcon2 40W to adjust the spot size according to engraving and cutting requirements. Therefore, the laser engraver is particularly well suited to cutting thicker objects with a full-power laser spot, and engraving and cutting thinner objects with a small spot.
The Falcon2 40W offers adjustable laser spot size.
The Falcon2 40W also offers optimized usability and safety. The integrated air-assist function not only offers stepless adjustment, but can also automatically adjust the airflow through LightBurn software to meet different cutting and carving needs.
The air assist function can also blow away dust during the engraving process, ensuring cleaner and smoother surface cutting, while maintaining quality and accuracy when engraving complex patterns. Smoke and dust can also be blown away, protecting the laser head lens.
The Falcon2 40W's integrated air-assist function that can automatically adjust airflow. 
The laser beam generated by the Falcon2 40W's powerful power output also offers personalization capabilities. When stainless steel is heated by the engraver's super powerful laser beam, the metal surface physically reacts to produce hundreds of colors, allowing for a more vivid end product.
The Falcon2 40W 25000mm/min engraving speed compared to alternative options. 
In terms of usage, the Creality Falcon2 40W supports offline adjustable preview, which can accurately locate and adjust engraving without connecting to a computer, again adding to the laser engraver's efficiency and convenience. Using the control panel, users can short press to fine tune 1mm, and long press to adjust 10mm/s. The Falcon2 40W also supports offline use, with no internet connectivity requirements. Once a TF card is inserted, users can create anytime, anywhere.
The Falcon2 40W's offline use capabilities. 
The Creality Falcon2 40W also offers a triple monitoring system for greater user control. Airflow Monitoring allows the user to adjust the airflow based on engraving needs. Additionally, the built-in Lens Monitoring system triggers an alarm when the lens becomes too dirty, helping to avoid lens breakage and frequent replacement. Flame monitoring is also incorporated, which triggers an alarm and immediately stops the laser engraver if a flame is detected.
The Falcon2 40W triple monitoring system. Image via Creality.
Five additional safety protections are added to the Falcon2 40W for greater security and peace of mind. The bidirectional limit switch ensures that, if the laser hits the boundary, the laser engraver will stop automatically and a buzzer will sound an alarm. An active stop function is also added, automatically stopping the Falcon2 40W in case of accidental tilt, flip or drop, sounding an alarm and sending an alert in the process. A security lock design, emergency stop button, and laser protective cover are also incorporated for added safety and security.

title: 🛠 Laser cutting Insulation material with the Creality Falcon 2
description:
During the renovation of my house, insulation material had to be adjusted in several places so that chimney pipes and air extraction pipes could be placed through the insulation material. Since it is very difficult to draw a perfect ellipse by hand, and even more difficult to cut it out with power tools, I used my Creality Falcon 2 laser engraver to create the holes. As a result, the holes are cut so cleanly and beautifully that it seems as if this was done directly in the factory of the insulation material.

The advantage of the Creality Falcon 2 compared to my other laser cutting machines is that the combination of the large power of 22 Watt and the perfect Air Assist make it possible to cut white sheet material without many burn marks being visible on the surface of the plate material.

title: Creality Laser Enclosure Tent Fume Extraction and LED Lighting Upgrade
description:
In this video we will be looking at the Creality Laser Enclosure Tent. I will walk you through the assembly and how to effectively use this enclosure to capture and evacuate and filter the smoke and fumes from the laser cutting process. This enclosure will fit over various popular machines such as the Creality Falcon 2 and the XTOOL D1 Pro plus many more.

I have made several upgrades and accessories for this enclosure to improve your user experience and address some of the enclosure shortcomings. 

The first is the LED lighting kit to better illuminate the inside of the enclosure. The Creality Laser Enclosure has a generous sized viewing window but due to the orange filter color it becomes difficult to see inside without a light source inside of the tent. This LED upgrade kit provides you with two LED light bars that securely mount to the enclosure frame and provide a daylight color temperature for comfortable viewing. The kit also includes all of the connectors and power supply for the LED bars. You can find it here:

► https://embracemaking.com/products/cr...

Additionally, the Creality Laser Enclosure only comes with a very small under powered fan. It will not produce the required pressure to effectively move smoke and fumes from the enclosure. To improve the ability to evacuate the unwanted fumes, I have designed a filtration system that can be used with the Craftsman "Bucket Head" shop vacuum. A HEPA and carbon filter can be fitted to the vacuum which now provides ample flow and pressure to move the fumes through longer hoses. There are also 3 and 4 inch hose adapters to fabricate your ideal fume extraction system. 

Craftsman Bucket Head Filter Adapter:
► https://embracemaking.com/products/fu...

Hose Adapters:
► https://embracemaking.com/collections...

Overall the Creality Laser Enclosure Tent is one of the most reasonably priced laser enclosures on the market and has the largest access window and viewing panel. The materials appear to be of good quality and should not rip or tear. Creality claims that the material is flame retardant for obvious safety reasons. 

I would recommend this solution for covering your laser cutter and engraver - no matter the brand. I have personally used it to cover my Creality Falcon 2 and my XTOOL D1 Pro with great results. The overall dimensions are 700mm x 720mm x 400mm

title: Building a Large DRSSTC | Part Two: Extreme Testing (Propane, Plasma Globes, and More!)
description:
After spending the last seven years working my way up the Tesla coil food chain, I've finally completed my very first true DRSSTC, and now it's time to test it! 

Coil specs:
Secondary coil: 6" acrylic tube, 16" winding height composed of 34AWG magnet wire coated in epoxy. Roughly 60kHz with the 16" topload.
Primary coil: flat "pancake" coil with 8.75 turns, 16" outer diameter, 8" inner diameter
Resonant capacitor: 0.25uF/6kV bank of fifteen 942C20P15K-F Cornell-Dubilier capacitors (five parallel rows of three in series)
IGBT inverter: CM300 full-bridge, 1uF/800V snubbers on each module
Bus supply: 680VDC voltage doubler made from two 3300uF/450V electrolytic capacitors and an IXYS 1kV/30A "mini-brick" twin diode. Takes 240VAC (or 120VAC for 340VDC on the bridge).
Driver: Loneocean's UD2.7C, powered by a 24V/5A power supply. 
Interrupter: based on Steve Ward's burst-mode interrupter, but without the burst mode. It can reach 280us pulse times, but I never push the coil beyond 150us. Typical BPS frequency is around 100-200Hz.

title: Unlock the POWER of Laser Engraving | Creality Falcon2 40W - Fast, Precise, Painless
description:
Creality's new 40W Falcon2 laser engraver is a brilliant tool for folks like me and you who don't want to get involved in the geeky details. It feels like a complete product, not a half-finished Kickstarter project like some lasers.  It's compact, light and solidly engineered. Compared with a CO2 , it's lower cost, portable and doesn't need water cooling. I was about to buy one for my business when Creality offered to send me a Falcon2 40W plus enclosure and honeycomb bed. Serendipity or what eh? Marvellous.

In this episode I have a first look at the precision of the cuts, kerf widths, slewing speed and dimensional accuracy, using sub-micrometre precision gauge/gage blocks, a granite surface table, height gauge and dial test indicator to find if the claimed precision is delivered in a real-world implementation.

title: Clothes Wringer Restoration - Water Damage Restoration
description:
In this video, I restore an antique clothes wringer made by Anchor Brand in the US in 1898. 
More about the restoration: 
When I saw this piece for sale on a sales website, I knew from the start that it would be the subject of an exciting restoration video. This Clothes wringer is quite rare; only a few have been preserved due to their size, but also the fact that they are mostly wood, which has been subjected to water contact for many years at a time. 

The restoration process went well, with no problems but with great surprises. I didn't expect to find the wood so rotten on the inside. However, I kept all the original elements and restored the water-damaged wood. 
I cleaned everything very well and then applied a wood treatment, after which I used a thick coat of wood putty, which I sanded after drying. I also applied a coat of paint for long-lasting protection. 
The parts of the wood on which the engraving was still visible were retouched by hand, and the elements on which the engraving had disappeared were re-engraved using a laser.

I worked on this antique clothes wringer with much love and patience over three weeks and am thrilled with how it turned out. It works and is now saved and stored well. It probably ended up in the landfill if I hadn't stepped in. 
Please ask me if you have any questions about what I used and why. I answer everyone!

More about the antique Clothes Wringers: 
In 1888, Ellen Eglin invented her groundbreaking device, a particular type of clothes-wringer, which was a machine that had two wooden rollers attached to a crank; after being washed and rinsed, wet clothes were fed between these rollers and an immense amount of water was squeezed out. The clothes were then hung to dry, which took significantly less time due to the wringer. Although the design was perceived as a popular product well into the 20th century, Eglin received very little credit or financial success for her invention. 
The wringer I restored was made in Erie, Pennsylvania, USA. 

If you have more information or one just like it, please write to me! Also, remember to subscribe for future restoration projects!

title: From Scratch: DIY Front Suspension & Gearbox Using Creality Laser
description:
Ciao ragazzi pronti per tornare a scuola guida ?!?!😂 Io ho sempre sognato di costruire un differenziale a ingranaggi, per osservare come funziona  anzitutto e adesso con un incisore laser (Creality Falcon 2) tante idee possono diventare realtà, e un modello in miniatura di un cambio automobilistico potrebbe essere un mio futuro progetto, per questo progetto in plywood ho impiegato 10 giorni di disegni per il modello 3D da me disegnato.
La parte più difficile del progetto? I giunti cardanici a destra e sinistra, bisogna costruire il giunto e lasciarlo libero, in modo che il centro di rotazione delle ruote venga trovato dal giunto stesso, altrimenti si forza il giunto a lavorare in una posizione di tensione/compressione e semplicemente non ruota!
Spesa sostenuta? 10 euro (10 dollari), il costo dei 10 cuscinetti su Amazon !!

(Hi guys ready to go back to driving school?!?! I have always dreamed of building a gearbox differential / front suspension, to observe how a differential works and now with a laser engraver (Creality Falcon 2) many ideas can become reality (creative project), and a miniature model of an automotive gearbox could be a future project, for this plywood project took me 10 days of drawings for the 3D model I designed.
The hardest part of the project? The universal joints on the right and left, you have to build the joint in order and leave it free, so that the center of rotation of the wheels is found by the joint itself, otherwise you force the joint to work in a tension/compression position and simply not wheel!
Expense incurred? 10 euros (10 dollars), the cost of 10 small bearings on Amazon!!)

title: I built a huge RC Global Hawk Drone - but does it fly?
description:
Hi Everyone!
In todays video I am building a huge 1-16 Jet Powered Global Hawk Drone. This project is a continuation of my Ardupilot series and it combines many new interesting solutions  like V-Tail, Flaperons, Skis and Electric Jet Thruster. It was also my first time building such a large plane, so I might have messed some things up. The whole Global Hawk weighed around 1200 grams with 5S Battery and 1500 grams after adding the Skis and balance bolts at the rear. With the EDF able to produce more than 2kg of thrust I had assumed there would be no problems with taking off, but it seems I was wrong. It’s possible that the Li-ion batteries together with weak ESC were limiting the thrust, or maybe the shape of tail was pointing the thrust downwards due to Coandă effect.
But most likely it just needs a long and smooth runaway and proper landing gear in order to achieve take off speed. I will definitely revisit this project once the snow melts, but before that I would be very thankful for your advice and ideas on how to make this plane actually fly.

Hello everyone,

In this episode I review the Creality Falcon 2 22W laser engraver.
Diode lasers have developed impressively over the past few years, and this machine from Creality represents a massive leap-forward in terms of utility and quality of life features.
The 22W laser is powerful, and ideally suited to the needs of scale model makers.  The impressive 25000mm/min top speed is class leading and helps get engraving jobs completed quickly.

The stand-out feature for me though is the integrated air-assist, a feature often lacking in machine of this class.  It helps to keeps the cuts/engravings clean, it allows thicker materials to be tackled.  In addition, the air-assist helps to keep the laser lens cleaner, this increases cutting efficiency and reduces maintenance downtime.

I am often asked which laser cutter would I recommend to a beginner.  To date, I've felt unqualified to answer the question as my experience has been with CO2 lasers, which come with operational challenges such as tube fragility, time consuming (and sometimes expensive) maintenance, as well as fume extraction challenges.
My experience of experimenting with the Falcon 2, has changed my perceptions of diode lasers generally, and I would thoroughly recommend this machine for these reasons.

1. Excellent, user focused design.
2. The pre-assembled frame makes set-up and tear-down a 5 minute task.
3. The built-in safety features make the process very safe indeed.
4. Everything required to get started is in the box, and the set-up guides provided make the process very straightforward indeed.
5. The packaging and instruction manuals are excellent, and it is simple to re-use the packaging to store the machine after use.

In the video I make use of the optional honeycomb table and optional enclosure.  I'd recommend both.  The honeycomb work table is especially well made and superior to the one on my CO2 laser, I was genuinely impressed when I took it out of its box.  :)

To be clear, Creality sent me this machine to review, so do your homework before considering any purchase.  But I can honestly say that this machine is excellent and has exceeded my expectations, and changed my view of the usefulness diode laser machines.  If you are new to laser engraving or cutting you would enjoy the simplicity of set-up and ease of use of this machine.  I look forward to preparing more videos in the future using it, and showing just how simple it can be to go from an idea into production.

Thanks for watching,

James

title: The Creality Falcon 2 40W Laser - Impressive Cutting Power
description:
40W lasers are everywhere, but are they all equal?  In this video, I will look at the Creality Falcon 2 40W laser to see how it stands up to the competition.  This is a laser with blistering 40W cutting power, but it retains a few old-school features.  So, is it up to the task?  Join me to find out.

UPDATE NOTES:
1. At 1:31 in the video I claim that the maximum speed is 25000mm/s and it should actually be 25000mm/min.  Also Creality tells me that it is possible to adjust the maximum speed by making adjustments in GRBL settings and they claim it can easily be set to 36000mm/min

2. It is possible to adjust the laser power for cutting/engraving by setting the GRBL parameter $156 between 0 and 1 to adjust the power from Lightburn.

3.  Regarding the air assist.  Creality tells me that it is possible to set the air flow low for engraving or high for cutting from within Lightburn, so the manual adjustment knob on the side is only to allow for specific manual settings as required.

title: Is Creality's Falcon 2 Pro Laser Engraver Really New And Improved? (A Saveitforparts Review)
description:
Last year I reviewed the original Creality Falcon 40W laser engraver and had a few concerns about it. This year, Creality has a new upgraded version, the Falcon 2 Pro. They've fixed a lot of the issues I had, including a much better enclosure and improved airflow and reliability. 

The laser is very powerful and fast, I was able to do most of my engraving and cutting projects in under an hour per design. 

The included 1.6W low-power laser as a great bonus, and engraves much more detail on delicate surfaces than the main 40W laser. 

The only real downside of the Falcon 2 Pro are the built-in material support slats. They aren't as good as a traditional honeycomb support, and don't allow materials to be held down. For any warped or heat-sensitive materials like wood or plastic, the slat system doesn't work very well. 

The smoke extraction and safety features on this were great. The addition of a built-in webcam and internal light were also really nice improvements, and overcome some common issues of other lasers.

It was very challenging, like always, but rewarding. I learned a lot about bread cutters.
The blade was highly rusty, with a considerable layer of rust that required extensive hand sanding and patience to regain its usable shape. 
I encourage you to watch this video to learn more about this antique German bread cutter.
When I saw it, I was impressed at how bad it looked. It was full of rust, layers of random paint, and a few cracks. The wood was utterly gone and eaten by time and bugs. 
The most challenging part was the crack repair. This time, I chose to do it differently—a method anyone can use. This is especially true since cast iron is hard to fix, and not everybody has a welding machine or knows how to use the brassing method. 
The most beautiful part was the woodworking after cleaning, repairing, and painting everything. I chose pearwood as the hardwood for this project.
The wood was cut and engraved with a Falcon 2 Engraving and Cutting Machine; if you want to learn more about it, you can do it here: https://s.zbanx.com/r/QX6jpI9ekWjk
Use code: NEWFALCON
I loved the results, and the burnt wood effect on the sides was terrific. Then I applied some Swedish wood oil, and the pear wood started to show its unique texture. 
After the blade was cleaned and polished, I assembled the old bread guillotine and made a test for you! It worked perfectly!  

I hope I have caught everything, but if you have any questions, you can comment, and I'll get back to you! I always do! 

Cheers! Johnny.

title: How to make AMAZING LASER engravings on CERAMIC with TiO2 | I used the 40W Creality Falcon 2
description:
My laser engraver (Falcon 2 40W from Creality): https://store.creality.com/eu/product...
You can use the code: VDFALCON9(€500 OFF)
 https://s.zbanx.com/r/2oI6LmKYDiu1
You can use the code: FALCON

In this video I show you how I make laser ENGRAVINGS on CERAMIC with TITANIUM DIOXIDE (TiO2) and a LASER CUTTER. The engravings on this material are usually not very marked and are hardly noticeable (especially the photos)...so for this I use TiO2, which is a chemical compound that is widely used in the manufacture of ceramics due to its ability to cause a physical and chemical effect on it and then when removing the titanium dioxide by burning with the laser, it leaves a mark or "stain" that is quite visible and dark (which is our engraving with a perfect and well-marked effect) without need of using a lot of power in our machine. title: Setting up and testing out the Creality Falcon 2  22w laser engraver and cutter.
description:
This is the Creality Falcon 2 laser engraver and cutter.
This was 22 watt Falcon 2 unit was sent to me by Creality to test out.

Now, this is not the normal kind of tool I'm used to dealing with, but I do love trying out something new. 
I am not familiar with laser engravers, so I was a little nervous about testing this out and figuring out how to work it. 
I shouldn't have worried. This unit was so simple to set up and use.
Literally only needed to take it out of the box, screw on some feet, slide on the laser, and start cutting. 

This is a fantastic piece of kit, very user-friendly, very easy to use, and very powerful. And this is only the 22w laser. They also have a 40w laser.

1 mistake I made in this video is the maximum cutting capacity. It is not 6mm but actually 15mm. My mistake was for not fully reading the spec sheet or manual. 

For the price of this unit, I was expecting it to run quite slowly, be very loud and not overly accurate, especially with curves. 
But apon opening the box, I knew right away my expectations were wrong. 
This thing cuts so fast and moves so smoothly and accurately. 
You can tell how smooth and accurate it is when cutting curves or circles. CNC units like this can not actually move in a curve. They move the laser in a zigzag motion using very small small steps. A smoother curve requires a smaller step. The smaller the step, the greater the accuracy. As you can see from cutting the circular jigsaw, this moves seamlessly.

I am very impressed by this falcon 2 engraver and see why lasers like this are becoming so popular with hobbyists and small businesses.
Once you start, you are always looking for and thinking up new projects make. 
I know I'll be using this unit more and more, as I was only planning to do a quick unbox and test using the micro ad card. 
But I actually went out and purchest a brand new laptop so I could start making my own projects on it. Plus, im very tempted to buy rotary roller attachment for engraving cylindrical items. 
But I think I'll have to master the lightburn software more first. 

Check them out. Well, worth the money of your looking to buy a laser engraver.

title: S2 E35 A Laser Cut Model Railway Turnout using 3d Printed Plug Track Chairs
description:
Hello everyone,

It had been my intention to take January '24 off from making videos and focus upon developing a set of tutorials for the excellent Templot Plug Track.
I've made a good start, and you can see the progress of the pages here:
www.85a.uk/bexhillwest/wordpress

More material will be uploaded over the next couple of weeks following this video release.

Anyway, a question on the Templot Club forum, from a member who is modelling in 3mm scale, prompted me to have a go at making an experimental turnout in 3mm scale using a laser cut track base.  Whilst doing so I thought it might make for an interesting video and here is the result.  It's much smaller than I'm used to, but even so, the quality of the 3d printed chairs is excellent.  They're really strong.  I used Anycubic ABS-like V2 resin to print the chairs.

Now, as I was putting the video together Martin Wynne (Templot's creator), has announced that the next update will include some changes which will improve the experience I show here.  But even so, I thought what I had still provided some useful insight so I've kept the video as-is.
Once the update is released I'll make the necessary changes to the tutorial website so those wishing to experiment for themselves should be able to find up-to-date information.

Finally, on Sunday 28th January 2024 I will be at the Longfield Model Railway show, on the South Eastern & Chatham Railway Society stand.  If you're passing and fancy a chat do please come and say hello.  I'll have some Plug Track bits and pieces with me if you'd like to see some examples in-person.

My best wishes,

James

Since my last laser-cut speaker project, which was 4 years ago, I’ve always wanted to get my hands on a laser engraving machine, so I’m excited to see what Creality can offer with the budget-friendly Falcon 2. The laser comes pre-assembled and well protected with many accessories included like the material sample kit, a honeycomb bed, raisers for additional height, tools for assembly, laser safety goggles, an air assist pump for cleaner cuts and even a rotary roller for engraving cylindrical objects. The laser module itself has a power of 22 Watts and Creality claims it can cut through 15mm of wood in a single pass. The laser module has built-in cooling fans, three warning lights for the air assist, fire detection and lens contamination. The frame can fit on most desks making it a great option for hobbyists and has a large working area of 400*415mm. Considering the price and the fact that it fits on a desk, I think this is a powerful tool for any workshop. I’m excited to have this laser engraver at my disposal to help me realize many of the projects I have in mind.

✅ get Lightburn (free trial for a month), then 60€ for a license (with coupon "NEW-10" its 50€!) https://de.atomstack.net/products/lig...
✅ ensure that the focal length of the laser module is correct and the lens of the laser module is clean when powered off (It can be cleaned with cloth and alcohol)
✅ parameters are for reference only because the color of the material is different and it will lead to a different effect
ENGRAVE: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Iw-0...
CUT: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IvIZ...
✅ higher power or slower speed means deeper cut
✅ lower power or faster speed make shallower effect (engrave)
✅ on brushed stainless steel can achieve colorful effects by setting different parameters, but the oxidation degree of different materials is different, and slight differences in focal length and power will also affect the actual effect. It is recommended to do some tests on your material
✅ the bottom surface of the cutting place should be suspended (use honeycomb worktable or the included rods) when cutting 
✅ protect your workbench (using aluminum plates or other materials that are not easily penetrated by laser)
✅ disable “Air” when engraving / enable ”Air” when cutting

title: Testing the Creality Falcon 2 22 Watt Laser Cutter - Second Review
description:
Today, we have a laser review for you.  You can see more of my videos here:    • Turnings  .

I'm talking about the Creality Falcon 2, 22 watt laser cutter that redefines precision and efficiency in the world of laser cutting.  Click below to save and order yours today.

In today's video, we'll be putting the Creality Falcon2 through the paces and testing more of the claims.  We will start with attempting to color stainless steel, as the claim states.  I sourced two pieces of 1mm brushed stainless steel to test the claim.  The laser does indeed color stainless as Creality claims.  However, my butterfly example did not come out with the same colors as the material test piece using the same parameters from that piece.  This could have been partly my fault for a couple of reasons.  One of which is my knowledge, or lack thereof, within the Lightburn software.

I also reviewed the enclosure that came in the bundle.  The enclosure goes together easily and quickly.  More importantly, it keeps the smoke from the laser contained, which is what it is designed to do.  The only drawback to the enclosure is the exhaust fan included with it.  It is weak in the CFM department and doesn't move air quickly enough to be of much use in a production environment.  If you have the time to wait for it to clear the smoke, it does work.  Just not so much for my needs.  That said, paired with my more powerful smoke extraction fan, this is not an issue.

In addition to the above, I used the Falcon 2 to create a rather elaborate layered owl.  The laser cut and engraved it quickly and beautifully!  I am very pleased because now I can do more of this sort of thing much much faster than before.

Lastly, I wanted to review the rotary device that came with the bundle.  I did this using two items/materials that I had not initially intended on using.  The first was engraving on glass.  The rotary functions as advertised and the laser did this very well.  I will be using this capability much more.  The second was engraving on a powder coated stainless tumbler.  I was very happy with the result, even though I failed to size the artwork properly.  Again, this is partly due to my inexperience with the software.  I hope to do more of this sort of thing as well.

All in all, I have to say, the Creality Falcon 2 laser has met or exceeded all my expectations.  The precision and speed at which it cuts through materials is truly impressive. It has definitely elevated the quality of my products.

With its reliable performance and exceptional cutting capabilities, the Creality Falcon 2 22 watt laser is a game-changer in the world of laser cutting. If you're looking for a machine that delivers on precision, efficiency, and quality, then look no further.
